title: The Ceremony Starts at Four
tagline: Two hundred guests, a ceremony that starts at four sharp, and a vendor who just stopped answering their phone.

wake_up.text: Wedding day. The timeline is printed, laminated, and taped inside your binder — and it never survives contact with reality quite the way it's written.

choices.text: Call every vendor for a final confirmation before you even leave
Trust yesterday's confirmations and head to the venue

venue_arrival.text: The venue is empty and quiet, exactly the calm before the day fills it with two hundred people and a great deal of feeling.

choices.text: Begin setup

random_moment.text: Setup mornings have their own small, unpredictable texture — a little different at every wedding.

choices.text: The venue staff turns out to be unusually helpful today
A minor linen color mixup needs sorting out
The weather forecast just improved for the outdoor portion

florist_delivery.text: Flowers arrive, mostly right — one arrangement is noticeably different from what was ordered.

choices.text: Rework the arrangement yourself with what's on hand
Let it go — it's close enough and there's a lot left to do

bridal_party_arrival.text: The bridal party arrives for hair and makeup, nerves already running high. Someone's asking you a question every ninety seconds.

choices.text: Stay present and handle every question personally
Delegate most of it to your assistant and keep working setup

vendor_crisis.text: The photographer, confirmed twice this week, isn't answering calls or texts. Ceremony is at four. A backup photographer exists, but booking them now means real cost and real risk of a different style than the couple chose.

choices.text: Book the backup photographer immediately, no more waiting
Keep trying to reach the original photographer a little longer
Tell the couple immediately and let them help decide
Ask the venue for their go-to backup on short notice

vendor_outcome_backup.text: The backup arrives with forty minutes to spare, professional and ready. The couple never even needs to know how close it came.

choices.text: Brief the backup photographer on the day's shot list

vendor_outcome_wait.text: The original photographer finally calls back — car trouble, genuinely unavoidable, and now genuinely too late. The scramble for a backup happens with far less runway than it should have had.

choices.text: Scramble for a last-minute replacement

vendor_outcome_transparent.text: The couple, to their credit, takes it in stride and trusts your judgment on the replacement. Being honest with them early turns a crisis into a decision made together instead of a surprise sprung on them.

choices.text: Move forward with their input

vendor_outcome_venue.text: The venue's go-to photographer happens to be available and is already familiar with the space — a genuinely lucky break that comes together faster than expected.

choices.text: Confirm the arrangement

ceremony_prep.text: Guests are arriving. The processional order needs a final check, and the officiant has one last question about timing.

choices.text: Triple-check every detail before the ceremony starts
Trust the plan you've already built and let it run

ceremony.text: The ceremony begins, exactly on time. Whatever happened this morning, none of it is visible from where the two hundred guests are sitting.

choices.text: Watch it come together

reception_setup.text: While the ceremony wraps, the reception space needs to flip fast — tables, lighting, the band's soundcheck, all in under an hour.

choices.text: Oversee the flip personally, detail by detail
Trust the setup crew to handle it and take a breath

end_shift.text: The reception is in full swing, the couple on the dance floor, and for the first time all day, there's genuinely nothing left for you to fix.

choices.text: Head home

triumphant.title: The Wedding They'll Never Forget
triumphant.blurb: Every call today was the right one, including the one nobody but you will ever know about. This is the wedding other planners hear about.

steady_hand.title: Flawless Execution
steady_hand.blurb: No visible hiccups, no stressed-out couple — just careful, competent planning from setup to send-off.

ordinary_day.title: Another Beautiful Wedding
ordinary_day.blurb: A full wedding day, pulled off. Nobody in the room knows how much work that actually took, which is exactly the job.

burned_out.title: Running on Fumes
burned_out.blurb: You made it to the send-off, but there's nothing left in you. This pace, wedding after wedding, has a real cost.

written_up.title: A Hard Conversation
written_up.blurb: Something about today's handling is going to need explaining to the couple, or the venue, or both.
